verdict.rationale: Cursor's rules and Automations documentation directly deliver this story: project rules (cursor-docs-35) encode standing behavior, hooks (cursor-supp-hooks) trigger on defined lifecycle events (preToolUse, afterFileEdit, beforeShellExecution, etc.) to run scripts and gate actions, and Cursor Automations (cursor-supp-automations) run cloud agents on schedules or in response to GitHub/GitLab/Slack/webhook/Linear events, with the /automate skill letting users describe triggers in plain language. Webhooks (cursor-supp-agent-webhooks) further confirm event-driven automation. missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification that rule-triggered automation reliably fires as configured, and clearer detail on rule-based (vs hook/automation-based) event triggering specifically.
